kept.heading: AUDIENCES DON'T WANT MORE FOOTAGE. THEY WANT IN (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Studios respond to fan demand with more content, but audiences are looking for participation, not passive viewing. Fans raised on games and creator culture remix, extend, and interact with story worlds. Data shows deeper fans want new ways into a franchise, not just more of the same. Companion formats like podcasts keep attention but lack agency. The real gap is participatory infrastructure, and the next phase of entertainment will let fans actively shape worlds between releases.

kept.heading: THE SHIFT FROM SEO TO SOCIAL CONTENT (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Search intent isn't disappearing, it's being intercepted before it reaches a company's website. AI overviews answer the query directly inside Google, and GenAI assistants like ChatGPT and Perplexity now guide most B2B buyers through research and shortlisting without a single visit to a vendor's blog. That interception is why SEO leads that once arrived weekly now arrive monthly, and why the fix has to happen on the social platforms and communities where B2B buyers now spend that research time instead. The way through is repurposing what SEO already built, turning the case studies, reports, and articles into video, carousel, and thought leadership formats.

kept.heading: TV ADS FOR B2B - WHY IT WORKS AND WHERE TO START (5 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: TV advertising is becoming a viable growth channel for B2B as digital ads get more expensive and saturated. Connected TV lets companies retarget existing audiences with 15 to 30 second storytelling, often using repurposed content like founder videos or customer testimonials. Budgets can start small, around $50 per day, and performance improves once traffic scales. TV also lifts other channels, with reported gains like a 25% increase in branded search. Test early and treat TV as a long-term, compounding channel.

kept.heading: I CAN'T BELIEVE SOME MARKETING TEAMS SKIP THIS (5 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Customer census surveys are an underused marketing motion that helps teams collect customer insights and build a stronger evidence library. The best surveys are cross-functional, tightly scoped to around 10-15 questions, and targeted to active users for higher-quality responses. Treat the send like a campaign with follow-ups and incentives, then move quickly on responses to turn feedback into testimonials, reviews, and advocacy opportunities.

kept.heading: SAUCE (TOOL)
kept.blurb: Sauce helps teams measure and prove how off-site and creator-led content drives AI visibility and search performance. It shows which posts appear in engines like ChatGPT and Perplexity, who created them, and for which queries. A 7-day free trial is available.

kept.heading: BUILD A HERMES INBOX TRIAGER IN 90 MINS (10 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: This guide walks through building a Gmail triage agent with Hermes and the read-only IMAP tool Himalaya. The agent sorts incoming mail into five labeled folders, scores each by urgency, and pings Slack only when something crosses a genuinely urgent threshold, staying silent otherwise.

kept.heading: WHEN AI CHATBOTS BOOST VS HURT SALES (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: AI chatbots work best when shoppers need help comparing products or sorting through large assortments. Across four experiments with 1,339 people, chatbot recommendations increased purchase intention by 44.7% for products that are hard to evaluate, such as apparel that varies by fit, size, and style. Chatbots also increased engagement for simple products that have many options, but reduced purchase intention for simple products that have small assortments because they added unnecessary friction. Use chatbots where they simplify complex decisions and organize choices instead of adding another step to an easy purchase.

kept.heading: ANTHROPIC WILL PAY ITS NEW STANDARDS EDITOR $300K TO ARGUE ABOUT COMMAS (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Anthropic is hiring a Standards Editor for around $300K to oversee grammar, tone, and clarity across its communications. The role highlights a broader trend as AI makes content generation cheaper and human judgment more valuable. While models can produce endless drafts, companies still need editors who can protect brand voice, simplify complex ideas, and decide what is worth publishing. The hiring trend suggests editorial judgment is becoming a premium skill in an AI-driven content market.

kept.heading: DJI USED GOPRO TO KILL GOPRO (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: DJI used GoPro's brand to make consumer drones easier to buy, then replaced GoPro by building the complete product itself. The GoPro mount gave DJI product validation and customer demand without camera R&D or category education. DJI walked away after GoPro asked for two-thirds of the profits because it believed flight technology created a stronger competitive advantage than cameras. DJI then launched four new drone generations over 30 months while GoPro built a competing product, which let it stay years ahead before GoPro's Karma drone failed and left the market.

kept.heading: HOW POLAROID IS WINNING GEN Z BY REJECTING AI AND SCREENS (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Polaroid recodes film's slow development and lack of editing as premium benefits, mindfulness, authenticity, pitting one unrepeatable print against an iPhone's vault of near-identical shots.

kept.heading: IS THE AGE OF READING ACTUALLY OVER? (5 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Nearly 400 independent bookstores opened in 2025, and print book sales are higher than a decade ago. Readers also spend more time with books daily than they did twenty years ago. Claims that reading is dying dismiss this growth as niche while treating declining attention spans as proof of collapse. Yet people still consume more words across digital formats. The shift is intentionality. Long-form reading is becoming a deliberate choice, raising the bar for creators to earn sustained attention.

kept.heading: CONTENT IS NO LONGER ENOUGH (5 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: As content becomes more saturated, brands are focusing less on producing more and more on building communities. Dentsu, NFL Mexico, and Warner Bros. Discovery argue that fandom and belonging create stronger connections than reach alone. Audiences want to participate, not just consume, making creators and fan communities valuable partners. The opportunity for brands is to build spaces where people can engage with shared interests beyond the content itself.

kept.heading: +39% CONVERSIONS BY REMOVING A PROMINENT CALL-TO-ACTION (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Removing a prominent homepage CTA increased conversions by 39% because it guided first-time visitors through the service before asking them to request a quote. The original CTA sent people straight to a form that asked technical questions many could not answer, so many left before converting. The updated journey introduced service details, trust signals, and expert credentials before visitors reached a quote CTA on the relevant service page. Match each CTA to the visitor's level of understanding so the next step feels simple and appropriate instead of asking for a commitment too early.

kept.heading: STOP MARKETING TO STRANGERS (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Most marketing over-focuses on acquiring new audiences while neglecting people who already know you. With declining external traffic, visitors now arrive with context, yet brands still treat them like strangers. The real opportunity is “step-two” marketing, guiding engaged users toward clear next action and deeper content. Growth comes from improving experience, not just reach. Small execution gaps like broken promises or poor follow-through quietly erode retention over time.

kept.heading: USE AI TO FIND YOUR FASTEST ROUTE TO CULTURAL TRACTION (WEBINAR)
kept.blurb: Attention today goes to the brands that are part of the conversation, not the ones interrupting them. In this webinar, Vanina Schick will walk through how to connect your brand into POVs with strong cultural energy and use AI to find where you can enter cultural conversations online. It will take place on July 23 at 9 AM PT.

kept.heading: THE 2026 PAID PLAYBOOK: AUDIENCE, CHANNELS, AND AI (12 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: AI made producing ads nearly free without creating any new attention to fill, so more ads now chase the same finite audience and simply raise the price of being seen. That moves the advantage to the audience layer, which a competitor cannot reverse-engineer the way it can copy creative or messaging. Resolving buyer identity before uploading lists opens the cheaper broad-reach channels that most B2B teams avoid, and running holdout experiments alongside attribution reveals which channels actually drive incremental conversions.

kept.heading: NETFLIX: THE BATTLE FOR ATTENTION (5 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Netflix spent years dismantling scheduled television, and now it's rebuilding pieces of the same bundle it once disrupted. Live sports, third-party channels, and short-form video are being layered in to turn the app into a daily habit rather than a destination for a single hit show. The tentpole approach, a handful of NFL and MLB games instead of full season packages, produced six of Netflix's 10 largest sign-up days over five years despite consuming just over 5% of content spending. If those additions do not feel cohesive, Netflix risks becoming the bloated bundle it once replaced.

kept.heading: THE $400,000 CHIEF OF STAFF IS THE CEO'S SECRET WEAPON IN THE AI AGE (5 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: AI-era CEOs are increasingly hiring chiefs of staff as strategic partners, not just assistants. The role has grown as leaders face greater complexity, with chiefs of staff helping execute initiatives and build workflows. While AI may automate some administrative tasks, skills like judgment, communication, and influence remain difficult to replace. The position is also becoming a leadership pipeline, with many chiefs of staff moving into executive roles.

kept.heading: ENGLAND VS THE INTERNET: WHAT DID REDDIT MAKE OF THE NIGHT IT ALL FELL APART AGAINST ARGENTINA? (6 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Redditor sentiment often evolves through debate and social proof instead of a single viral opinion.

kept.heading: NETFLIX SAYS LIVE EVENTS BOLSTER ADS BUT AFFECT VIEWER ENGAGEMENT (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Netflix is using live events to win subscribers and grow ad revenue even though they generate fewer total viewing hours than on-demand content.

kept.heading: ZARA'S ‘DEATH PANTS' ARE TRENDING BECAUSE PEOPLE KEEP TRIPPING ON THEM (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Zara's wide-leg pants became “death trousers” after viral injury videos turned a design flaw into a social media trend.
